{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: How can I help you today?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my professors that they don't see me as a human with real emotions and feelings.
supporter: I understand that you are feeling like your professors don't see you as a person with feelings. What happened to make you feel this way?
seeker: I have testing all the time and study non-stop, but the professors don't seem to encourage or support me.  They just see me as a number I feel.
supporter: That's hard to feel like they are treating you like a number when you are working so hard.  Have you talked to them about it?
seeker: It's hard to trust them when I'm seen as 1 of 100 people.  If I am struggling they don't flinch or ask me how they can assist.  I just am expected to 
seeker: tough it out.
supporter: I had a similar experience in my college days. It was very difficult to have so much pressure to succeed and feel so alone.  You can do though because you are working hard and want to succeed.
seeker: Thanks for the encouragement.  Where do I start to help myself feel better?
supporter: I see you are anxious about this when talking to you, but have you thought about getting some support from other students in your position?
seeker: That sounds like a good idea.  Maybe they are feeling this way too.
supporter: Also sometimes just stepping back and taking some deep breaths can help to alleviate some anxieties. Have you tried that ever?
seeker: I will have to give that a try.  I've done that in the past and had forgotten just how much that helped me before.  
supporter: That is reassuring that it worked before for you and  can work again.
seeker: I'm so worried about failing because I just don't feel the support from my professors to care either way for my successes.  It's so different from high school and home when my parents encouraged me and supported me full-heartedly.  
supporter: College can be quite a change from the protective atmosphere of home.  Have you tried any support groups or religious groups for encouragement?
seeker: I am religious so perhaps I could seek a group out and they could help with encouraging me.  
supporter: I was a  part of a religious group in college and they were very supportive even praying for me on exam days.  I felt they helped me with my success by planting seeds of positive feedback to me.
seeker: I used to be part of one during high school years, and that sounds like it would help.
supporter: Are you starting to feel better about the situation?
seeker: Yes, I do thinking about other people filling in the gaps and supporting me when others won't or can't. Thanks for chatting.  This was helpful.
supporter: You are welcome.  I wish you well.
seeker: I think I have a few tools now to make things better.","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-07-15","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello
supporter: How are you doing today?
seeker: hello
supporter: How can I help you?
seeker: I need ways alleviate stress while studying 
supporter: It sounds like you are having some difficulty at school, I have definitely been there.
seeker: yeah, it can be tough sometimes and feel like you're in a dead end situation
supporter: Yes I worked a dead end job for ages when I was younger and sometimes you just feel stuck
seeker: How did you push past that job?
supporter: I am going to be honest a little luck was involved I managed to impress a customer that came in and ended up applying at their work.
seeker: Are you still with that job now, enough to consider it a career?
supporter: I would say so I am an insurance broker, it has only been a year or so but there seems to be room to move up. You can find something too
seeker: Is there any advice for getting out of my situation?
seeker: aside from luck that is
supporter: Can you give me some more details?
seeker: I just find the work mundane and way too remedial 
supporter: That is completely understandable
seeker: did you look at any websites or other job searching tools before you found your new job?
supporter: I have you a few, there are also many ways to gain skills online that buff up your resume a bit
seeker: what types of skill can I gain online?
supporter: Indeed is one of the better ones to look for jobs, honestly I would suggest looking at jobs that you normally wouldn't and see what kind of qualifications they need and see if you can get that done online.
seeker: so filter based on my absolute needs and go for online skills that I can complete?
supporter: yes I think that is a great idea, look for jobs that meet your needs and figure out what you can do to look attractive to employers
seeker: I have tried glassdoor before, have you had any luck there?
supporter: I used it a bit, I mainly used indeed.
seeker: and have you showcased your skills using LinkedIn before? I have had that one recommended to me before, they said its a great way to neatly organize accomplishments and personal background
supporter: Yes especially if you are applying for anything in a professional setting that is very important.
seeker: do you have any examples of online skills you completed?
supporter: coursera has a lot of great courses, it really depends on what you are looking for.
seeker: if I was looking to enter the engineering field, any recommendations?
supporter: Is that what you are going to school for?
seeker: yes but I may change my mind
supporter: What year are you in? most engineering programs have a practicum and that is a great opportunity to make contacts and potentially get offered a job
seeker: yes I have been networking as I go
supporter: Honestly you seem like you are pretty on top of this I don't think you will have any issues finding a job.
seeker: yeah I mean the topic was about final exam stress but we got on a tangent
supporter: Yes that is fair enough, how much time do you have until your exam?
seeker: 15 minutes
supporter: While that is plenty of time to get some studying done:)
seeker: yes I probably should, thank you for your insight!
supporter: Honestly I find that if you are going for the test right away I always like to just breath and relax a bit.
seeker: yeah no use in cramming for more info when I could just chill out
supporter: You seem like you know what you are doing, I think you will do just fine
seeker: yup thanks","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-25","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

{"full_source_conversation":"supporter: Hello there! How can I encourage you today?
seeker: Hi, I have been going through a lot of stress with school and am also sad and lonely as of late and not sure how to make myself feel better
supporter: So you have had a lot of stress with school lately and are struggling to keep yourself cheerful?
supporter: Is there something in particular at school that is stressing you out? Exams? Relationships?
seeker: Yes! Its very hard to keep positive with all the work I have and I feel I am not doing well.
seeker: Yes, I have a lot of exams right now and that on top of not hanging out with friends a lot lately has made life tough.
supporter: I can understand being stressed if you think you are not doing well in school and have a lot of work. How are your grades now?
seeker: I still have decent grades but I feel like I am not prepared for big exams currently and they are worth a lot
supporter: Yes, that can be tough. When I had a lot of tests coming up and a lot to study for, I wrote down goals to study -- like I broke down the classes and made certain goals to study a bit in each class. And then if I did that, I could go out with friends or some reward like that. 
supporter: For example, if you have 7 classes, you can make a chart for when you will study for each of those classes and then check them off as you accomplish it, maybe not all in one day, maybe break it up in reasonable bits. Then study according to your goal, if that makes sense.
supporter: I remember after each class, I would take 15 minutes to review all my notes from class, that seems short, but really, it adds up and helped so much.
seeker: Yes, I think you have excellent advice about organization. I feel like I lose track of what I have and when to do it. I also bounce between classes, feeling stressed because there is so much. Do you think doing one class at a time is best?
seeker: I also tend to save stuff sometimes so I have a lot of work build up with tests on the same days. I am not sure how to stop procrastinating.
supporter: Yes, stick to one subject at a time. For example, if you think 1/2 hour is good enough to study, then stick to that. When done, your done until the next time it is on your schedule.
seeker: Ok. Thank you so much for the ideas. It seems like you have had similar experiences with stress from school.
supporter: Procrastination never makes us feel good. If I keep putting something off, I then feel guilty. If I make a goal, and I reach it, I can put a reward. For example, if you study 3 subjects 1/2 hour each, you can go out for yogurt with a friend. So you reward yourself for sticking to that goal.
supporter: Yes, I did. lol I'm really old now. This technique I use in all my life. Even house chores, I break it down into a schedule, put it in writing, then check off what I do. Then I feel good about my accomplishments.
seeker: Yes, that was my other question to you. It sounds great to just do a little time for each class but I often get overwhelmed and need a break
seeker: I have never used check lists or planners. I think it is part of how I get overwhelmed maybe.
supporter: Definitely you need a break, so schedule them as rewards. You can even do 15 minutes in say 4 subjects, then take a walk, take a cup of tea, or call a friend, then back to the books. 
supporter: Keep it as SIMPLE as possible, don't get bogged down. I used to think planning was TERRIBLE< but actually, it sets one FREE. You feel so much better and accomplished when you see how much you have done. It really is amazing. 
supporter: HOw man classes do you have?
supporter: many *
seeker: I have 6 classes
supporter: That's a lot but it is totally doable. Here is a good example, If you plant seeds in a garden today, you have to weed it a bit tomorrow, the next day, the next day, you have to wait for rain, then weed some more, the harvest comes and YAY! You are happy. But if you lie on your bed, never planting, never weeding, you procrastinate, you get nothing.
supporter: If you write your classes down and then write a reasonable time to study each one. Maybe 3 today, 3 tomorrow, then add rewards if you do that, maybe make a list of rewards, so you can pick and choose, then you check off when you do the subject.  Like a chore chart. 
seeker: Yes haha. That is a good comparison. You have been super helpful. I will for sure try to use your advice. Thank you!
seeker: Have a great day and thanks again
supporter: You are quite welcome! God bless have a great day!","kind":"MS","reported_at":"2024-06-10","schema":"pm-rl1-attributed-evidence-v2","speaker_scope":"Historical seeker and supporter; neither role supplies an AI biography."}

turns.content: Hey Andrew, how have you been doing lately?
Not too great, to be honest. Things have been a little rough with my friends.
I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about it?
Yeah, I confronted them about how they haven’t been inviting me to things, and it didn’t go as I hoped.
That must have been really hard for you. What happened when you talked to them?
Well, some of them seemed surprised and apologetic, but others kind of brushed it off or got defensive.
It's understandable that you're feeling upset about that. How did their reactions make you feel?
I feel really hurt by the ones who brushed it off. I thought we were closer than that.
